chunks: Muhammad, from Abdullah bin Muhammad, from Ali bin Al-Hakam, from Aban bin Uthman, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The most superior of the charities is cooling a parched liver (quenching one's thirst).
ai.seo_question: What is considered the best form of charity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), identifying 'ibrad al-kabd' (cooling the parched liver) as the pinnacle of charity, a phrase rooted in classical Arabic poetry to denote intense thirst. This hadith elevates the physical act of providing water from a mere social courtesy to a supreme spiritual merit, reflecting the Shia emphasis on tangible, bodily relief (khususiyya) as a direct path to divine pleasure.
